supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:28 UTC, FILE-NWD-01 opened an HTTP connection to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080, with 640,000,221 bytes recorded from the file server to the proxy. This is consistent in scale with the alert.
A second, much smaller HTTP connection from FILE-NWD-01 to the same proxy was recorded at approximately the same time.

The large transfer’s size is consistent with the inventory description of approved StratoSafe backups, but the available flow record does not identify the destination service or the process that generated it.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-NWD-01 winsec and Sysmon logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the alerted transfer; the process, account, and job responsible therefore cannot be established from those sources.
PROXY-NWD-01 proxy logs were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so the requested URL or upstream destination and proxy-side transfer details are unavailable.

The available Zeek connection record shows the internal proxy as the destination, but does not establish the ultimate external destination or that the transfer was made by the approved StratoSafe agent.
claims_not_established: Whether the 640 MB transfer was generated by the approved StratoSafe backup agent or another process.
Whether the proxy forwarded the transfer to stratosafe-backup.com or to an unapproved destination.
Whether the transfer contained authorized backup data or data being exfiltrated.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover PROXY-NWD-01 logs for the transfer, including the request host/URL, authenticated identity, and upstream destination.
Obtain FILE-NWD-01 process, service, and scheduled-job records for the transfer interval, including evidence of stsync.exe execution and backup status.
Correlate proxy or firewall records with the 640,000,221-byte flow to determine its ultimate destination and transfer outcome.
unrelated_findings: A domain controller record at 13:43:51 UTC shows a Kerberos service-ticket request for svc-archive from public IP 139.162.174.124. This is unusual and warrants separate investigation; the available records do not establish that it was connected to the alerted transfer. (T040-00193)
